key_insight: Thermal drawing replicates a multimaterial cross-section over kilometres per hour with no lithography. What carries over is litho-free cross-section replication, not woven memory fibres.
killer_doubt: Weavable fibres are >=10 um wide, so a woven crosspoint cell is ~100 um2 vs DRAM's 0.0017 um2: 1e4-1e5x less dense. Chalcogenide channels need in-fibre crystallisation even to work.
decisive_experiment: Not worth $1M. A <$100k check: draw a 50 um fibre with 16 crystallised-Se coaxial cells, weave a 16x16 mat, and measure access time and retention. The density ceiling follows from fibre pitch alone.
prior_art: Fink (MIT) and Sorin (EPFL) multimaterial fibres; Fink's 2010 metres-long in-fibre chalcogenide p-FET made by in-situ crystallisation (via search snippet).

key_insight: Graphoepitaxial DSA on coarse 193 nm guides, plus SIS conversion of the dots, could give EUV-free 10 nm-pitch device sites. Worth keeping as a patterning module, not as this cell.
killer_doubt: A 10 nm-pitch planar MIM (5x5 nm, k=40, 5 nm) is ~2 aF, about 11 electrons at 1 V; charge-transfer sensing needs ~0.5 fF, 250x more. Diodes cannot write 0s.
decisive_experiment: For <$150k: make DSA+SIS dot arrays in guided trenches and measure dot-placement defects per cm2 and single-dot rectification by conductive AFM. A capacitor of >=0.3 fF at 10 nm pitch must close on paper first.
prior_art: DSA dot and contact-hole patterning (IBM, imec, Intel, MIT Ross/Berggren PS-PDMS); Argonne sequential infiltration synthesis; diode-access crosspoint memories (3D XPoint, Samsung diode PRAM).

key_insight: Data that dies before the cell loses it needs no refresh at all. A runtime that tags allocation lifetimes could run a short-retention tier refresh-free.
killer_doubt: Accelerator DRAM holds mostly weights and KV cache living seconds to hours; training activations live ~0.1-1 s. Sub-ms data is likely <10% of capacity, already in SRAM.
decisive_experiment: Instrument HBM allocations in PyTorch training and vLLM inference traces, then histogram lifetimes weighted by capacity and by traffic. Revisit only if >30% of capacity lives <2 ms. Under $50k.
prior_art: RANA (ISCA 2018): refresh-optimised eDRAM that skips refresh for short-lived CNN data; RAIDR/Flikker refresh relaxation; gain-cell eDRAM (Teman/Giterman); imec IGZO 2T0C.

key_insight: Stack-and-draw copies one preform cross-section into thousands of identical vertical devices per slice with no scanner. A litho-free transistor faceplate is a fresh, capital-light concept.
killer_doubt: Thin co-drawn layers break up by capillary instability; the best uniform drawn features are ~40 nm. A GAA access array needs ~3-5 nm dielectric at <=30 nm pitch.
decisive_experiment: In a Fink/Sorin-class draw tower (<$300k), co-draw a Ge- or Se-core, glass-clad, metal-gate coaxial preform. Measure dielectric continuity against thickness after 1e3-1e4x reduction, and Ion/Ioff of microtomed slices.
prior_art: Fink (MIT) 2010 in-fibre chalcogenide FET; EPFL ultimate drawn feature sizes, uniform down to ~40 nm (via search snippet); NRL nanochannel-glass stack-and-draw arrays.

key_insight: Folding puts single-crystal lateral transistors in every tier from one planar process, avoiding the channel-quality limits of deposited 3D tiers.
killer_doubt: Each tier's area is still lithographed separately, so cost per bit is planar (1x) plus fold yield loss; 3D pays only when one etch patterns all tiers. Registration is ~um.
decisive_experiment: Start with a $0 cost model: folding leaves processed wafer area per bit unchanged. If a footprint-limited niche survives (HBM), fold a 50 nm SOI strip 8 times and measure metal continuity across the fold lines and transistor shift.
prior_art: Rolled-up/origami nanomembranes (Schmidt at IFW Dresden, X. Li at UIUC); Smart Cut layer transfer and CEA-Leti sequential 3D give c-Si tiers with nm alignment.

key_insight: Re-scoped: a CMOS-under-array sense amp per 4k-cell tile refreshes locally, keeping refresh off global bitlines and bandwidth. Insurance if 3D oxide tiers retain only 1-64 ms hot.
killer_doubt: As stated (10 pA, ~50 us retention), even 1-5 fJ per local refresh costs 0.17-0.86 W/GB in standby vs ~0.012 W/GB for DDR5; a 1 TB server burns 170-860 W.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus a 28 nm MPW tile (metal caps emulating 4k cells, leaky TFT models) to measure fJ/bit per local refresh and tile availability. Pair it with 85-110 C retention maps of stacked IGZO tiers. About $300k.
prior_art: CMU subarray-level parallelism and refresh-access parallelisation (Kim, Chang); gain-cell eDRAM with us retention (Teman/Giterman); Micron CMOS-under-array in 3D NAND.

key_insight: Liquid-metal skin transfer lays down a 1.5-3 nm wide-gap oxide at room temperature, with no vacuum or hydrogen: a possible low-capex channel for planar BEOL tiers.
killer_doubt: imec IGZO 2T0C already retains >400 s, so lower leakage buys almost nothing. Planar transfer cannot coat the 3D holes or recesses where 3D DRAM channels live.
decisive_experiment: Print Ga2O3 and In2O3 skins onto 100 mm SiO2/Si, pattern 50 nm FETs, and map Vt and 85 C off-current uniformity against ALD IGZO controls. About $150k in a university lab.
prior_art: Zavabeti et al., Science 2017 (RMIT, Kalantar-Zadeh), liquid-metal printed 2D oxides; printed In2O3 TFTs (Daeneke group); Purdue's atomically thin ALD In2O3 FETs.

key_insight: Spatially separate trap pockets, read by swapping source and drain, give 4 bits per gate crossing: a real density lever if writes did not wear the dielectric.
killer_doubt: Hot-carrier and tunnel writes through nitride/oxide wear out at ~1e4-1e5 cycles. DRAM-class needs 3e8 (1 s refresh) to ~7e13 (hot rows), 1e4-1e9x more, and programming takes microseconds.
decisive_experiment: None worth funding as DRAM. A $50k cycling test of a double-gate IGZO/SONOS stack to 1e9 cycles at 85 C would confirm the charge-fluence rule.
prior_art: Saifun NROM and Spansion MirrorBit (including 4-bit/cell Quad); double-gate SONOS; Macronix 3D NOR/AND charge-trap flash.

key_insight: Storage nodes become floating gates on one shared vertical read channel, written through oxide transistors. No capacitor, no per-bit read contact, non-destructive read, and channel writes avoid charge-fluence wear.
killer_doubt: Each node still needs its own lateral write FET and write-bitline contact (Fact 2's blocker). With ~3 sublayers per tier and 0.1-0.3 fF nodes, read margin may be <100 mV.
decisive_experiment: Build a planar 8-node IGZO string in a university fab: series read TFTs whose gates are floating nodes written by IGZO write TFTs, plus coupling plates. Measure read selectivity, disturb, and 85 C retention. About $400k.
prior_art: No direct match in one search (via search snippet). Nearest: Toshiba NAND-structured DRAM (1990s), imec/IMECAS IGZO 2T0C, NEO 3D X-DRAM 3T0C, Kioxia OCTRAM.

key_insight: Retention-tail statistics are locked inside three firms. Standardised test structures shared across U.S. university fabs would let outsiders iterate on access devices, oxide TFTs especially.
killer_doubt: Tail cells matter at the 1e-6 to 1e-9 quantile of a 1.7e10-cell die. Millions of pooled 1 um cells reach only ~1e-6, with different physics (no GIDL or single-trap tails).
decisive_experiment: Pilot in two university fabs: run one oxide-TFT test chip carrying 1e5-cell retention arrays twice, and check fab-to-fab tail agreement before scaling up. About $400k.
prior_art: SkyWater SKY130 open PDK (with Google); NSF NNCI university fabs; CHIPS Act NSTC/Natcast shared facilities. None of these targets access-device leakage tails.

key_insight: A photodiode gated by the storage node is a light-powered keeper: one global flash tops up only 1-nodes, refreshing every cell with zero activations and no refresh hammer.
killer_doubt: The cell becomes 2T1C plus a photodiode (>=2x area) to recover 10-20% of bandwidth. At 1-10 mW/cm2 a 0.003 um2 cell gets only ~14-140 fA; stray carriers discharge 1-nodes.
decisive_experiment: On a 65 nm BSI image-sensor MPW, build 1k self-gated photodiode keeper cells. Under illumination, measure the 0-node upset rate and 1-node hold against flux at 85 C. About $250k.
prior_art: None found for optical refresh. The inverse, DRAM as image sensor (Micron OpticRAM, 1980s), is old; electrical self-restoring 3T/4T loadless cells need no optics.

key_insight: A two-terminal selector plus a planar MIM at each crosspoint gives transistor-free 4F2 decks at KrF. An 80 nm-pitch MIM holds ~0.45 fF, enough with charge-transfer sensing.
killer_doubt: At us-ms retention every OTS switches 1e3-1e6 times/s: 3e11-3e14 cycles in 10 years, beyond OTS endurance. ~1000 half-selected cells at ~nA sneak swamp a sub-fC read.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate 1S1C crosspoint test arrays (GeSe OTS plus TiN/ZrO2 MIM) at a university fab. Measure hold leakage at Vth/2, read signal against line length, and OTS cycling to 1e12 at 85 C. About $300k.
prior_art: 3D XPoint OTS selectors (Intel/Micron); selector-only and self-selecting chalcogenide memories (SK hynix, Micron); 1S1R crosspoint stacks.
